paragraphs.source_en: Seeing Nobumoto fall silent, the young Nobuchika believed his brother had yielded. But how could he know that words cannot truly change another person, and that victory in argument sometimes merely exhausts the loser’s patience? Nobuchika did not understand this, and unwittingly committed a foolish error. Nobumoto would never submit to this glib-tongued younger brother. His patience had already reached its limit.

paragraphs.source_en: A twisted age bred twisted character. In this blood-soaked age of turmoil, blood relatives slaughtering one another had long ceased to be remarkable. Survival demanded schemes of every kind. In that sense, there was no difference between commoners who toiled daily for food and fuel and daimyō raised in ease and luxury.

paragraphs.source_en: To Nobumoto, who believed that only by siding with the Oda could they survive, his brother had become the greatest threat. If he resolved to side with the Oda, Nobuchika would surely draw his blade against him. Yet when he thought of eliminating Nobuchika at the Kuma residence and killing two birds with one stone, a chill ran repeatedly down his spine. He too felt the sorrow of kin killing kin, but this age of chaos permitted no sentimentality.
